fixes.explanation: The One on the throne says, “To the thirsty I will give freely from the spring of the water of life.” Freely, friend. That means given, not sold. I have been thirsty for less than this.
Nothing in the verse mentions a desert or a dark sky. John says, “Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth…” The passage even says there will be no more night in the city (Revelation 22:5).
John doesn't see an empty sky. He says he saw “…a new heaven and a new earth…” and he adds that the sea was no more. So the heaven and earth he sees are new. Empty is not the word, baker.

The One seated on the throne is the one speaking. He says, “Behold, I make all things new.” ALL things, friend. Not some things, not just the top shelf, ALL. I'm a stamper who got made new, so I'm a little biased, but that might be my favorite line in the whole passage.
Great is a word I'd happily use for Him, baker. But the One seated on the throne says, “Behold, I make all things new.” The word is new. Say it with me, new. ALL things.
The stars light up MY sky, one for every finished cookie box. But the city isn't shining with starlight. The text says it's “…shining with the glory of God.”

Elders do show up elsewhere in Revelation (Revelation 4:4), but this verse doesn't name them. It says the foundations bear the names of “…the twelve apostles of the Lamb.” The word in the blank is apostles, friend.

The verse doesn't give that as the reason. Revelation 22:3 says the throne of God and of the Lamb will be within the city, and His servants will worship Him. The reason for no temple is that the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple.

John says the opposite. He says, “Its gates will never be shut at the end of the day, because there will be no night there.” Never shut, friend. My bakery has a CLOSED sign I flip every night, but those gates never get shut at the end of the day.

Gold and jewels are all over this city, friend. The street is pure gold, and the foundations are adorned with every kind of precious stone. But the verse says only those whose names are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life enter.

John was carried away in the Spirit to a mountain great and high, where he was shown the city (Revelation 21:10). But Revelation 22:1 says the river is “…flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb” The throne is the source, baker.

On either side of the river stands a tree of life. And that tree has twelve kinds of fruit and a fresh crop each month. A tree that gives a fresh crop every month is my kind of kitchen. I'd just keep walking back to it.
